method: Analytical enumeration exploiting cost differential: since cost_Y (3) < cost_X (5), maximize Y subject to constraints. Derive Y >= ceil(1000/2)=500 from balance constraint at X=0; then iterate Y from 500 upward to find minimum feasible (X,Y). Alternatively, iterate Y in valid range and pick minimum 5X+3Y. Key insight: Y is cheaper per unit, so optimal solution has Y as large as possible.
steps: Parse constraints: X+Y>=1000, X-2Y<=500, X,Y>=0 integers
Derive analytical bounds: Y in [0,1000] (from X>=0 and X+Y>=1000)
For each candidate Y (0..1000), compute X_min = max(0, 1000-Y) to satisfy effectiveness
Check if X_min satisfies balance: X_min - 2Y <= 500
Return X, Y, and total cost

method: Standard MILP formulation with Highs solver: integer variables X,Y, minimize 5X+3Y subject to X+Y>=1000, X-2Y<=500, X>=0, Y>=0. Use mip_rel_gap=0 for exact solution.
